Debt Crisis Grips India’s Industrial Intermediate Prod Sector; Century Extrusions Ltd Among Firms Hit

A mounting debt crisis has engulfed India’s Industrial Intermediate Prod industry, sending shockwaves through its key firms and manufacturing sites. The crisis, sparked by a sudden tightening of credit lines from non-banking financial institutions, has left several companies unable to refinance maturing obligations or fund day-to-day operations, according to industry sources.

Century Extrusions Ltd, one of the sector’s prominent players, confirmed on Thursday that it is facing “acute liquidity stress” and has initiated talks with lenders to seek relief. “The abrupt withdrawal of working capital facilities has severely impacted our production schedules. We are operating at less than 40% capacity across our plants,” a Century Extrusions Ltd spokesperson told this newspaper.

Industry observers estimate that across the sector, dozens of facilities have scaled back output or suspended shifts, and at least 8,000 workers are currently on unpaid leave. “The credit freeze has created a ripple effect—firms are unable to purchase essential inputs or pay wages in full, leading to widespread uncertainty among employees,” said Sandeep Agarwal, secretary of the Industrial Intermediate Prod Association.

According to figures released by the association, outstanding debt across the industry has climbed by nearly 22% since last year, while average selling prices have dropped 15% due to weakened demand. “Without urgent intervention, we could see more companies default on their obligations,” warned Agarwal.

Union representatives reported growing unrest among workers, who are demanding clarity on wage payments and job security. “Our members are anxious about their future as factories slash output,” said Ritu Sharma, leader of an employee union at a major site in Gujarat.

With no immediate resolution in sight, the crisis continues to unfold, casting a cloud of uncertainty over the sector.
